diagnostic_evidence.quote: (\K, D(\K)) is the Koopman generator of a jointly continuous, global flow in $\Omega$.
In particular, Koopman semigroups induced by jointly continuous, global flows in a Polish space $\Omega$ are bi-continuous contractions in $(C_b(\Omega),\|\cdot\|_\infty,\tau).$

issues.failure_explanation: Condition (ii) requires (\K,D(\K)) to generate a bi-continuous semigroup 'with respect to $\tau$ induced by a jointly continuous flow', i.e. it presupposes the existence of the very jointly continuous flow whose Koopman generator is asserted in condition (i). The claimed equivalence is therefore circular: the substantive direction of the Dorroh–Neuberger theorem (a derivation that generates a bi-continuous semigroup yields a flow) is assumed away, and as stated the theorem no longer characterizes Koopman generators. The 'In particular' conclusion (bi-continuous contractions), which is what the paper actually uses in Remarks remApp and rem324, remains valid.

failure_location.quote: (\K, D(\K)) is a derivation (i.e., \K(fg) = (\K f)g+f(\K g) for all $f,g\in D(\K)$ and generates a bi-continuous semigroup with respect to $\tau$ induced by a jointly continuous flow.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the clause 'induced by a jointly continuous flow' from condition (ii), restoring the cited characterization: a derivation (\K,D(\K)) on C_b(\Omega) is the Koopman generator of a jointly continuous global flow iff it generates a bi-continuous semigroup with respect to $\tau$.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem no longer asserts the Dorroh–Neuberger characterization (the hard existence direction is circular), but no labelled result is invalidated because the paper only uses the 'In particular' bi-continuity statement, which is unaffected.
issues.title: Circular hypothesis in the Dorroh–Neuberger characterization (Theorem D-N)
issues.why_classification: A one-clause deletion restores the cited Dorroh–Neuberger characterization in full, and the only conclusion the paper uses (bi-continuous contractions) is unaffected, so no guarantee or dependent result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Three defects in the explicit content of Theorem thm:added-1. (i) The printed a_k is not a Yoshida composition root: for k=1 it gives 0.4236+0.2835i, which does not satisfy the required order condition 2a^3+(1-2a)^3 = 0, whereas the paper's own decimal a = 0.324396+0.134586i is the correct root; hence the recursion (HO53) as stated does not deliver order 2k+2. (ii) In the displayed W_{[1]}, merging the three copies of V_2 forces the middle factor e^{(1-a)t\K_2/2}, but the paper prints e^{(1-a)t\K_2}; the \K_2-exponents then sum to 3/2 - a/2 ≈ 1.338-0.067i ≠ 1, so the displayed scheme is not even a consistent splitting, contradicting the claimed order 4. (iii) In the displayed W_{[2]}, two \K_2-factors e^{(a+b)t\K_2} should be e^{(a+b)t\K_2/2}, and the central \K_1-coefficient is defined as d = 1-2a, while the recursion forces d = (1-2a_2)(1-2a_1) ≈ 0.0833-0.1471i — confirmed by the paper's own W_{[3]} decimals (e.g. h = 0.0137277-0.060005i uses this value). As printed, the \K_1-exponents of W_{[2]} sum to 1.7265+0.0114i ≠ 1. The errors propagate to the displayed W_{[3]}. The recursion, the order claims (2k+2), and the term counts (2·3^k+1) are correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the printed a_k formula by the correct Yoshida root a_k = 1/(2+2^{1/(2k+1)} e^{iπ(2j+1)/(2k+1)}) (equivalently, keep the printed decimals, which are correct), and re-derive the expansions of W_{[1]}, W_{[2]}, W_{[3]} from the recursion (HO53): halve the middle \K_2-factor of W_{[1]}, halve the two (a+b) \K_2-factors of W_{[2]}, and set d = (1-2a_2)(1-2a_1) ≈ 0.0833-0.1471i.
issues.overall_effect: The printed 4th-, 6th-, and 8th-order schemes are not valid splittings (they violate first-order consistency), so the 'In particular' claims of Theorem thm:added-1 fail as written and any implementation of the printed formulas does not approximate e^{t\K}; the numerical experiments' 4th/6th-order columns must have used corrected coefficients. The recursion (HO53), the order 2k+2 claim, and the 2·3^k+1 term counts remain valid.
issues.title: Invalid composition coefficient formula and wrong explicit expansions in the Yoshida-scheme theorem (thm:added-1)
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained but nontrivial: the defining coefficient formula must be replaced by the correct Yoshida root and several displayed coefficients re-derived (including the structurally wrong relation d = 1-2a), which is more than a typo fix; however the recursion, the order claims, and the term counts all survive, and the experiments' methods are correctable.

issues.failure_explanation: The 6th-order row of Table tabNterms (17, 145, 289, 1313, 2465, 3617, 4913) is produced by Algorithm alg:added-1 from the base value x = 17, but no 17-term order-6 scheme exists in the paper: the order-6 schemes constructed in Theorems thm:added-1 and splitU have 19 (W_{[2]}) or 33 (U_{[4]}, Z_{[2]}) terms, while 17 is the term count of the order-5 scheme U_{[3]} of Theorem splitU. Hence the entire row — including the three-dimensional value 145 behind the experiments' complexity discussion — is inconsistent with the paper's own theorems; with the consistent 19-term Yoshida base the correct entries are 19, 181, 361, 1819, 3439, 5149, 6939.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the intended order-6 base scheme — consistently with the 4th- and 8th-order rows, the 19-term Yoshida scheme W_{[2]} of Theorem thm:added-1 — and re-run Algorithm alg:added-1 from x = 19, replacing the row by 19, 181, 361, 1819, 3439, 5149, 6939; alternatively, if the 17-term scheme U_{[3]} was intended, the row must be relabeled as 5th order.

issues.title: Sixth-order row of the exponential-term count table rests on a nonexistent 17-term base scheme
